DataVivid 0.1.1 fixes copy and paste and adds the Linux build. It is the first release built automatically by GitHub Actions.

## Fixed

- **Copy and paste with other apps.** Copying cells (Ctrl+C or right-click > Copy) now reaches the system clipboard, so you can paste into Excel, LibreOffice or any other app. Pasting text from other apps into the grid works as well. In 0.1.0 the status bar said "Copied N cell(s)", but the cells stayed inside DataVivid.
- **The GitHub link in Help > About** now opens your browser.

## New: Linux build (x64)

- Runs on distributions with glibc 2.35 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, Fedora 36+, Linux Mint 21+ and similar), on X11 and Wayland.
- `install.sh` installs it for your user only (no sudo). It adds DataVivid to the application menu and to the file manager's *Open with* list, and makes it the default app for CSV, TSV, Parquet, JSON Lines, Arrow, Avro and SQLite. Use `./install.sh --no-default` to keep your current default apps.
- On Linux the *Windows* menu is called *Desktop*, and `datavivid --register`, `--make-default` and `--unregister` set up or remove the desktop integration.

macOS builds are still untested.

## Install

**Windows 10/11 (x64)**

- **Recommended:** download `DataVivid-0.1.1-windows-x64.zip`, unpack it, and run `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install.ps1`. This is a per-user install with no admin rights.
- **Portable:** download `datavivid.exe`, start it, and use *Windows > Register DataVivid for data files*.

The exe is not code-signed yet. If SmartScreen warns, choose *More info > Run anyway*.

**Linux (x64)**

```bash
tar xzf DataVivid-0.1.1-linux-x64.tar.gz
cd DataVivid-0.1.1-linux-x64
./install.sh                 # or ./install.sh --no-default
```

Remove it with `~/.local/share/datavivid/uninstall.sh`. The tarball also contains `datavivid.desktop` and `datavivid.png` for a manual or system-wide setup. For a portable install, download `datavivid-0.1.1-linux-x64`, make it executable with `chmod +x`, and run it.
